JUDGMENT

The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act through her natural guardian,
seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by her in the road traffic accident dated 06-11-2023.

2. The case of the Petitioner in brief is that: On 06- 11-2023 at about 4-15 p.m., the minor petitioner after alighting from the BMTC electric bus bearing Reg.No.KA- 51-AH-4539 at TTMC bus stop, Bengaluru -Mysuru main road and when was standing by the side of the road, at that time the driver of the bus by driving the vehicle in rash and negligent manner dashed against the petitioner, due to the impact she struck in between the bus and the cement barrier, result of which she sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately the petitioner was shifted to BGS Hospital, Bengaluru wherein first aid treatment was given and then she was shifted to Jayanagar Orthopaedic Centre, Bengaluru wherein admitted as an inpatient.
So far, the petitioner has spent sum of Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.
3. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
She was aged about 16 years.
She was student of 1st PUC at Sheshadripuram College, Bengaluru.
She was ambitious in pursuing her career as dancer and choreographer.
Due to the injuries sustained by the petitioner, she is unable to concentrate on her studies and unable to participate in cultural, sports and other activities.
4. In response to the summons, respondent No.1 did not appear before the court.
Hence he was placed Ex- parte.

5. Respondent No.2 - /the Insurer of BMTC electric bus bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AH-4539 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent no.2 has contended that the driver of the offending bus was not holding valid driving license and the said vehicle was not having valid FC and permit and that as per the police documents the alleged accident was occurred mainly Jayashree S vs Switch Moblility Automotive Limited on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69302435/
2 due to the negligence on the petitioner who negligently alightend from the moving bus hence the entire negligence is on the part of the petitioner but not on the part of the driver of the BMTC bus.

On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that, on 06-11-2023 at about 4-15 pm., when she was carefully alighted from the BMTC electric Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AB-4539 at BMTC bus stop, Bengaluru - Mysore main road at that time, the driver of said bus drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed her.
As a result of forced impact, the petitioner struck between the Bus and the cement barrier and she sustained grievous injuries ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as claimed?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom payable?
3. What Order or Award?
7. In order to prove the case, petitioner has examined her natural guardian/father Mr.Suresh M as PW.1 and one witness as P.W.2 and got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P19 and closed her side.
The respondent no.2 has not led any evidence.
8. Heard arguments of learned counsel for the petitioner and respondent no.2 and perused the entire materials placed on record.

9. My findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.
Issue No.3:

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to Ex.P9 which is the police records such as F.I.R, complaint, spot mahazar, sketch, notice u/Sec. 133 of MV Act, reply to the notice, IMV report, charge sheet, wound certificate etc.,
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by the father of the petitioner by name Suresh, case has been registered against the driver of the offending vehicle in Crime No.0377/2023 of Kengeri traffic Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279, 337 of IPC and u/Sec. 134 (a& b), 187 of MV Act.

After completion of investigation, the investigating officer has filed charge sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 279, 338 of IPC and u/Sec.
134 (a& b) r/w 187 of MV Act.
13.
The learned counsel for respondent no.2 has vehemently argued that the petitioner by alighting from the moving bus herself has caused for the accident and thereby contributed entire negligence.

14. In the light of the submission made by the respondent no.2 to the aforesaid effect, if the police records more particularly the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, the width of the road at the spot of accident is nearly 50 feet wide.

The respondent no.2 has contended that the petitioner has step down from the moving bus and that there was no bus stop near the spot of accident so as to alight from the bus at the stated place and that the rough sketch does not disclose about the existence of bus stop nearby the spot of accident.
15. It is true that in the spot sketch, the existence of bus stop near the spot of accident is not shown.
But if the spot mahazar is read in whole wherein it is clearly stated that the petitioner alightend from the bus at the BTMC bus stand.
It clearly revels that there was bus stop near the spot of accident.

Further when the offending vehicle is an electronic vehicle, there will be Automatic door and the said door will be opened only at the place where the passenger has to board the bus or to alight from the bus.
Hence, if there is no bus stand near by the spot of accident the automatic door of the bus would not have opened.

If it is opened at the place where there is no person to board or alight then it can be said that the said bus was not in a proper condition and if unconditioned bus is driven then negligence can be attributed against the driver of the said bus because when he is in the driver seat he has to see the condition of the bus before it is taken on move.
Hence, there is no reason to believe that the petitioner has alightend from the moving bus.

16. If the spot mahazar and sketch so also other documents are perused, the petitioner after alighting from the bus has tried to cross the road in front of the offending vehicle by crossing the offending vehicle.

If the cross examination of PW.1 is perused, wherein the counsel for respondent no.2 themselves have posed suggestion that the offending vehicle instead of plying the vehicle on the lane reserved for BMTC vehicle, has plied the vehicle in another lane meant for other vehicles and the being in bus in order to get down from the bus has jumped from the moving bus.

From the aforesaid suggestion posed by the Learned counsel for respondent no.2 coupled with the sketch which clearly reveals that the offending bus instead of using the lane reserved for BMTC bus has passed in the another lane.

Had the BMTC bus used the lane meant for it this accident would not have occurred because the petitioner has already crossed the lane meant for BMTC and when she was in the another lane so as to cross the road at that time this accident has occurred.

Hence, it can Jayashree S vs Switch Moblility Automotive Limited on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69302435/
4 be said that the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is the sole cause for the accident.

sentences.text: In the present case it is true that respondent no.2 has to taken steps to examine the driver of the offending vehicle but in spite of service of summons and repeated bailable warrant was issued but his presence was not secured.

When the witness who is the driver of the offending vehicle has avoided to appear before the court to give evidence, adverse inference has to be drawn against the case of the respondent no.1 because if driver of the offending vehicle was not at fault in causing the accident, he would have appeared and given evidence against to the case of the petitioner.

Hence,
the materials placed on record clearly proves the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver in causing the accident.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
17. Issue no 2 :
The guardian of petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his daughter/minor petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents which are at Ex.P.9 and P10.

On going through the medical documents it reveal that petitioner has taken primary treatment at BGS Global Institute of Medical Science & Hospital on 06- 11-2023 and then she was shifted to Jayanagar Orthopaedic Centre, Bengaluru wherein admitted as an inpatient from 06-11-2023 to 11-11-2023 for a period of 6 days.

entities.text: BGS Global Institute of Medical Science & Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
As per the wound certificate,
petitioner has sustained one injury which is grievous in nature.
18. Dr. B Ramesh -Orthopedic surgeon at Jayanagara Orthopaedic Center, Bangalore is examined as PW.2.
Through him Inpatient record and x-ray films are marked as Ex.P.18 and 19.
PW.2 deposed that he has examined the petitioner radiologically as to the assessment of disabilities.

PW.2 further deposed that petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability of left lower limb at 28% and whole body disability at 14% and further deposed that petitioner is said to be a student and the said disabilities will come in the way of her academic career.
PW.2 has deposed that petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants, which would cost around Rs.50,000/- to Rs.60,000/- in Jayanagar Orthopaedic Centre.
19. If the evidence of the PW.2 is perused, he is a treated doctor and it is he who has conducted surgery.
As per the evidence of PW.2 the fracture is united and that from the disability suffered by the petitioner it would not affect her academic career.
The PW.2 has assessed the disability at particular limb at 28% and to the whole body at 14%.

As per the judgment reported in 2014 (4)
Kar.L.J 157 Vijaya Kumar Alias Babu Rao Vs The Secretary, Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee Balki, Taluk the normal rule would be disability in the lower limb would be 1/3rd of the particular limb.

2014 (4)
Kar.L.J 157 Vijaya Kumar Alias Babu Rao Vs The Secretary, Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee Balki, Taluk

sentences.text:
Hence, the disability allegedly suffered by the petitioner would have to be 9%
instead of 14%.
From the document produced by the petitioner it can be gathered that the petitioner is Bharatanatyam artist and she has actively participated in scouts and guides.
The petitioner is aged about 17 years.
Hence there is very possibility of her recovering from the injuries sustained by her in the future days.

Though the percentage of disability suffered by the petitioner would cause some amount of discomfort and loss of amenities in life but there is no reason to believe that it would have direct impact on the future earnings of the petitioner.

Hence, this court instead of awarding compensation under the head loss of future income would inclines to award compensated under the head loss of amenities and discomfort to the tune of Rs.2,00,000/-.

sentences.text: Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained one grievous injury.

Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injury sustained by the petitioner and time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.60,000/- towards pain and suffering.

21. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner, she has produced 21 medical bills for the treatment taken by her at Jayanagar Orthopaedic Centre, Bengaluru for Rs.1,18,305/- at Ex.P.11.
Hence petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head medical expenses to the tune of Rs.1,18,305/-.
22. The guardian of the Petitioner has stated that they have spent considerable amount towards her conveyance and nourishment etc..
Therefore, Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.30,000/- under this head.

Thereby petitioner is entitled to the compensation as under:
Sl. Heads Amount No.
1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs.60,000/-

2 . Medical expenses Rs.1,18,305/-
3. Incidental Expenses Rs.30,000/-
4. Loss of amenities and discomfort Rs.2,00,000/-
 Total Rs.4,08,305/-

Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.4,08,305/- (Rupees Four Lakh Eight Thousand Three Hundred Five only ).
23.
As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that the offending vehicle was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of the offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no 2 this court directs the respondent no.2 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No. 2 is answered.
24. Issue No.3:
In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.4,08,305/- (Rupees Four Lakh Eight Thousand Three Hundred Five only) with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
